# gmail

Gmail - the Google adapter, split along its untrusted-input seams.

``provider.GmailProvider`` implements ``providers.base.MailProvider`` and
nothing wider. The package exists because the adapter sat at the
500-code-line ceiling, and every split here moved WHOLE functions out along a
real boundary rather than compressing working code (the one time compression
was tried it shipped an address-parsing regression, recorded in ``ids``).

The boundaries are the security story. Caller-supplied ids and header text
are validated in ``ids`` before any API call; a sent-mail selection becomes a
query only in ``query``, where ``in:sent`` is unconditional and every dynamic
value passes a validator before interpolation; wire payloads are decoded and
reply MIME encoded only in ``messages``, with every outbound header folded to
one line. ``provider`` owns the credential and the calls, and no other module
here touches either.

Key Components:
    - provider: ``GmailProvider`` - auth, read, label/move, flag, sent
      sampling, reply drafts. Scopes come from ``services.auth.scopes``.
    - ids: ``safe_id`` and address parsing for untrusted text at the edge.
    - query: ``users.messages.list`` query compilation, the ONE place a
      selection becomes a query string.
    - messages: pure codec - API dict to ``Message``/``SentMessage``, reply
      text to sanitized MIME.
    - history: ``users.history.list`` change feed and the cold-start
      bootstrap before a cursor exists.

Pattern/Convention:
    Construct through ``providers.get_provider("google", ...)``, never by
    importing ``GmailProvider`` directly. New code that touches the API goes
    in ``provider``; new code that decides what untrusted input MEANS goes in
    ``ids``/``query``/``messages`` and gets a boundary test beside the
    existing ones in ``tests/providers/gmail/``.

Example:
    >>> from inbox_zero_connector.providers.gmail.ids import safe_id
    >>> safe_id("18f3a2b4c5d6e7f8", "message_id")
    '18f3a2b4c5d6e7f8'

See Also:
    - inbox_zero_connector.providers.base: the interface and its absences.
    - inbox_zero_connector.providers.outlook: the Graph sibling; the no-echo
      refusal policy is shared and documented in ``ids``.
